 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 20, 2026, 21:31:36 IST SUMMARY The outlook for precious metals remains closely tied to the US monetary policy trajectory, currency movements and changing investor sentiment. Gold has faced considerable selling pressure, with a stronger dollar making the greenback-priced metal more expensive for buyers using other currencies. 
 Expectations of persistent inflation and further interest rate increases have also featured prominently in market assessments. Meanwhile, comments from Federal Reserve officials have reinforced expectations of tighter monetary policy, while futures markets have assigned a high probability to a December rate hike. 
 Beyond bullion, silver, platinum and palladium have also registered declines, pointing to weakness across the precious metals complex. Swiss gold exports have added another dimension to the market picture, with shipments recording a significant monthly fall. 
 Together, a combination of factors is expected to shape the direction of bullion market in the days ahead. Track TOI’s coverage to know which way gold and silver prices are headed: Live Events 
 LIVE RATES · INDIA ⟳ 4:54:05 pm Gold Rate 22K gold/gm ₹ 11,480 Silver Rate price/10gm ₹ 1,750 Platinum Rate price/10gm ₹ 38,560 21:31 (IST) Nov 20 Gold crashes to one-year low in India, loses Rs 17,600 in nine sessions Gold prices in Delhi plunged Rs 5,200 to Rs 1,29,300 per 10 grams on Friday, extending their losing streak to nine sessions and hitting their lowest level in a year, PTI reported. The metal has shed Rs 17,600, or 12 per cent, since November 9, amid a stronger US dollar, rising bond yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes. From its January record high of Rs 1.83 lakh per 10 grams, gold has fallen 29.3 per cent. 21:31 (IST) Nov 20 Silver crashes Rs 2.46 lakh from record high, loses 61 per cent in India Silver prices plunged another Rs 4,000 to Rs 1.58 lakh per kg in Delhi on Friday, taking its decline from the January 29 record high of Rs 4.04 lakh to Rs 2.46 lakh, or 61 per cent, PTI reported. Globally, silver fell more than 4 per cent to $41.12 per ounce, while gold dropped to $3,515.02 per ounce. Higher US interest rate expectations, a stronger dollar and elevated bond yields have intensified the selloff in precious metals.
 18:03 (IST) Nov 20 Gold selloff deepens as markets price in December Fed rate hike Gold extended its decline after Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson flagged inflation risks that could warrant another interest rate increase. Markets are now pricing in a 99.3 per cent chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool. Higher interest rates and Treasury yields make non-yielding assets such as gold less attractive to investors. Join conversation

 18:03 (IST) Nov 20 Gold heads for worst weekly fall in eight months as hawkish Fed outlook lifts dollar Gold prices fell for a fifth consecutive session on Friday, heading for their steepest weekly decline in eight months amid expectations of further US interest rate hikes. According to Reuters, spot gold dropped 1.3 per cent to $3,576.09 per ounce, after touching its lowest level since September 4, 2025. Bullion has lost around 8 per cent this week as a stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields weighed on demand. 13:54 (IST) Nov 20 Gold price today: Gold futures decline to Rs 1.22 lakh/10 gram Gold prices on Friday declined by Rs 4,683 to Rs 1,22,769 per 10 grams in futures trade amid weak spot demand. On the Multi Commodity Exchange, the yellow metal's contracts for December delivery traded lower by Rs 4,683 or 3.67 per cent, at Rs 1,22,769 per 10 grams in a business turnover of 11,730 lots. Analysts attributed the decline in precious metal prices to weak spot demand. Globally, gold futures declined by 3.53 per cent to $3,555.52 per ounce in New York. 09:13 (IST) Nov 20 Gold price today: Forced liquidation and inflation concerns add to selling pressure on gold Gold's sharp decline has also been accompanied by concerns over broader market liquidation, persistent inflation and rising yields. Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said there appeared to be some forced liquidation across markets in general. He pointed to expectations of imminent US rate hikes and the possibility of persistent inflation leading to higher yields and a stronger US dollar, both of which were putting pressure on gold. His assessment highlighted the combination of factors weighing on bullion rather than a single market trigger. With gold recording a weekly decline of around 8.9%, the precious metal faced pressure from changing interest rate expectations as well as movements in the dollar and broader financial markets. Spot platinum dropped 2% to $1,317 per ounce, while palladium declined 2.3% to $888.66 per ounce. Both metals were also headed for weekly losses. The declines came alongside a fall in spot gold, which slipped 1.9% to $3,551.68 per ounce, and a 2% drop in silver to $41.90 per ounce. The simultaneous weakness across the four metals marked a difficult period for the precious metals complex. Gold's weekly decline stood out, with bullion down around 8.9% and on course for its steepest weekly fall since the week of March 20. 09:12 (IST) Nov 20 Silver price today: Silver prices fall 2%, head for weekly losses alongside gold Silver prices also weakened alongside gold, with spot silver declining 2% to $41.90 per ounce. The metal was on course to record a weekly loss, reflecting the broader weakness across precious metals. Gold, meanwhile, had recorded a much sharper weekly decline of around 8.9%, its steepest fall in eight months. The movement in silver came amid a broader environment of a resilient US dollar and expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase. Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets, including precious metals. With silver also registering losses, the weakness was not limited to gold, as other major metals were also headed towards weekly declines. 09:11 (IST) Nov 20 Gold price today: Strong US dollar adds to gold's troubles, holds near 19-month high US dollar's sustained strength emerged as another challenge for gold prices, with the greenback holding close to a 19-month high. The dollar's recent rally made bullion, which is priced in the US currency, more expensive for buyers holding other currencies. This added to the pressure on the precious metal, which was already facing selling amid expectations of higher US interest rates. 
 A stronger dollar and rising interest rate expectations have featured prominently in the factors weighing on gold's performance. With the greenback extending its recent gains, currency movements remained an important factor influencing the international bullion market. The combination of a firm dollar and expectations of monetary tightening coincided with gold's sharp weekly decline.
 09:11 (IST) Nov 20 Gold price today: Gold heads for steepest weekly decline in eight months as prices hit September 2025 low Gold prices came under significant pressure, with bullion heading for its sharpest weekly decline in eight months amid a stronger US dollar and expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December. Spot gold fell 1.9% to $3,551.68 per ounce, after touching its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. 
 The metal was down around 8.9% for the week, marking its steepest weekly fall since the week of March 20. US gold futures for December delivery also witnessed a sharper decline, sliding 3.6% to $3,551.90 per ounce. The steep fall reflected the pressure on bullion amid changing expectations around US monetary policy and currency movements.
 Gold prices remain under pressure, with bullion facing a combination of a resilient US dollar, rising expectations of monetary tightening and higher interest rates. The precious metal has recorded a steep weekly decline, with spot prices touching their lowest level since September 2025. 
Expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike in December have emerged as a key factor shaping the outlook, with markets largely pricing in a 25-basis-point increase. Higher interest rates and elevated bond yields could continue to influence the appeal of non-yielding assets such as gold. 
Meanwhile, developments in international currency markets, Swiss gold export data and movements across other precious metals will remain important indicators to watch as bullion navigates a challenging market environment.
